ledger.why: the food and Farming effects on the ending page

items.text: The dish is comforting and delicious. The elder looks pleased.
The cook discovers that the elder has been omitting a crucial ingredient for years. They laugh about it.
The dish is plain but nourishing. The parent thanks the cooks and finally gets to eat.
The cook invents a delicious new dish.
The dish is spectacularly ugly but tastes wonderful.
The cook uses too much spice. Everyone drinks water and politely avoids a second helping.
The experiment fails. The cook salvages a simpler meal rather than wasting the whole harvest.
The child creates beautiful decorations from leaves.
The child carves a tiny face into a spare piece of cooked breadfruit. The elder calls it disrespectful. The parent calls it adorable.
The child makes a breadfruit crown and insists {@breadfruit_chief} of Breadfruit must be addressed properly.
The decorations are accidentally served as garnish. The cooks remove the inedible pieces before anyone eats.
Both recipes are delicious. The villagers enjoy the variety.
The elder's recipe wins narrowly. The cook requests the exact measurements for next time.
The new recipe wins. The elder is disappointed but asks for a small portion to take home.
A child prefers plain breadfruit and refuses to participate in the judging.
The feast is a success. Everyone gets enough to eat.
The cook and elder exchange recipes, with a few affectionate complaints about each other's methods.
The parent finally sits down with the baby and a warm meal. The entire village is ordered not to interrupt for five minutes.
The breadfruit sculpture is displayed for one afternoon, then eaten because it is, after all, food.
The cook admits that a meal doesn't have to be impressive to be worth sharing.

intro.name: The breadfruit
intro.text:
The village has harvested a particularly impressive breadfruit. It is so large that three villagers insist on measuring it.
A talented cook, (Cook), announces that (cook.he/she) will prepare a dish worthy of the Tree of Life itself.

question.name: Too many cooks
question.text: An elder, (Elder), insists the fruit should be cooked the old way. A child, (Child), wants to turn it into a sculpture. A parent carrying an infant would simply like everyone to stop arguing so the family can eat.

choices.label: LET THE CHILD DECORATE THE SERVING AREA.
MAKE TWO SMALLER DISHES AND COMPARE THEM.
